critical_code_review_comments: Fixes are minimal, surgical, and correct: (1) asyncio.get_running_loop() is the Python 3.10+ recommended API and guarantees the loop currently running the coroutine — this fully addresses the reported Selector-loop leakage on Windows 3.13. (2) Not rebinding state.semaphore inside start_batch() preserves the loop association established in register_batch() — this was the classic 'Future attached to a different loop' bug source.

No login logic, selectors, popup handling, or OTP flow bytes were changed — verified by mtime (only bulk_connect_worker.py modified) and by the fact that the two grep signatures for the fixes are the ONLY diff-worthy sites.

Recommendation for user: on Windows 11 + Python 3.13, also confirm `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsProactorEventLoopPolicy())` is set BEFORE uvicorn's loop is created (i.e. in an `if __name__ == '__main__':` guard before `uvicorn.run(...)`), not merely inside the FastAPI app import path — uvicorn --reload spawns a child process where policy set at import time may not apply.

rca of the issue: Two subtle asyncio loop-binding bugs in bulk_connect_worker.py could cause NotImplementedError at subprocess spawn on Windows 3.13 under uvicorn --reload: (1) asyncio.get_event_loop() (deprecated in 3.12+) can return a fresh default loop that is a WindowsSelectorEventLoop, which lacks create_subprocess_exec; (2) re-instantiating state.semaphore inside start_batch() bound the semaphore to whatever loop happened to be current at start_batch() call time (possibly a different loop than the one running _run_batch), causing Future-vs-loop mismatches that surface as NotImplementedError deep inside Playwright's driver spawn. Fix: use asyncio.get_running_loop() (line 500) and never rebind state.semaphore after register_batch() (lines 722-724). Both fixes verified present and correct; no other logic touched.
